title.narrative: AU-IBAR 2021-2024 Conserving Aquatic Biodiversity in Blue Economy
AU-IBAR 2021-2024 Conserving Aquatic Biodiversity in Blue Economy

description.narrative:
Syftet med denna insats är att förbättra AU-medlemsstaternas och regionala ekonomiska samhällens politiska miljö, regelverk och institutionella kapacitet att på ett hållbart sätt utnyttja och bevara den biologiska mångfalden och ekosystemen i vattenmiljön. Det handlar om att öka förmågan att ratificera och/eller anpassa den nationella politiken till internationella/regionala instrument som rör teman inom blå ekonomi, särskilt när det gäller att skydda och bevara den biologiska mångfalden. Insatsen kommer att stödja AU-medlemsstaternas kapacitetsuppbyggnad för att optimera bevarandet och den hållbara användningen av den biologiska mångfalden och samtidigt minimera konflikter mellan underteman inom den blå ekonomin. Under projektperioden kommer åtgärder för att mildra de negativa effekterna av kust- och marinturism, olje-, gasbrytning och klimatförändringar på den biologiska mångfalden och miljön i vattenmiljön att stärkas. Projektet har också ett specifikt mål att stärka könsinkludering i bevarandet av den biologiska mångfalden och miljöförvaltningen.
Insatsen görs efter en begäran till Sverige från ”African Union InterAfrican Bureau for Animal Resources” (AU-IBAR). Projektet stöder delvis genomförandet av den afrikanska blå ekonomistrategin som godkändes av Afrikanska unionen i oktober 2019. AU-IBAR har lett utvecklingen om denna strategi på uppdrag av Afrikanska unionen och ansvarar för att genomföra den i samordning med regionala ekonomiska gemenskaper och AU:s medlemsstater.
AU-IBAR kommer att vara avtalspartner till Sida och leda genomförandet av projektet genom att inrätta en projektimplementeringsenhet som kommer att ha personal med olika kompetens som behövs för att leverera de förväntade resultaten. AU-IBAR kommer att samarbeta med relevanta aktörer som icke-statliga organisationer och den privata sektorn i genomförandet av projektet. Projektet kommer att genomföras under en treårsperiod (2021-2024) med ett totalt svenskt bidrag på 46 877 000 kronor.

The aim of this contribution is to enhance policy environment, regulatory frameworks and institutional capacities of AU Member States and Regional Economic Communities to sustainably utilize and conserve aquatic biodiversity and ecosystems. It revolves around enhancing the capacity to ratify and/or align national policies with international/regional instruments related to blue economy themes specific reference to protecting and conserving biodiversity. The contribution will support capacity building of AU Member States to optimize conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity while minimizing conflicts among blue economy sub-themes. During the project period, measure for mitigating the negative impacts of coastal and marine tourism, oil, gas deep sea mining and climate change on aquatic biodiversity and the environment will be strengthened. The project also has a specific objective of strengthening gender inclusivity in aquatic biodiversity conservation and environmental management.
This contribution is made following a request to Sweden by the African Union InterAfrican Bureau for Animal resources (AU-IBAR). The project partly supports the implementation of the African Blue Economy Strategy which was endorsed by the African Union in October 2019. AU-IBAR has led the development if this strategy as mandated by the African Union and is responsible for implementing it in coordination with Regional Economic Communities and AU Member States.
AU-IBAR will be the agreement partner to Sida and will lead the implementation of the project by establishing a Project Implementation Unit that will have staff with various expertise needed to deliver the expected outputs/outcomes. AU-IBAR will liase with relevant stakeholders such as Non-Governmental Organizations and the Private Sector in implementing the project.
The project will be implemented over a period of three years (2021-2024) with a total Swedish contribution of SEK 46 877 000 (Forty Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy Seven Thousand Swedish Kronor).

The overall objective of the project is to enhance the policy environment, regulatory frameworks and institutional capacities of AU member states and regional economic communities to sustainably utilize and conserve aquatic biodiversity and ecosystems
The Strategic Objectives:
1. Ratify and/or align relevant international/regional instruments related to blue economy themes (with specific reference to protecting and conserving biodiversity)
2. Optimizing conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity while minimizing conflicts among blue economy sub-themes
3. Strengthening measures for mitigating the negative impacts of coastal and marine tourism, oil, gas, deep sea mining and climate change on aquatic biodiversity and environment
4. Strengthening gender inclusivity in aquatic biodiversity conservation and environmental management

description.narrative:
1.Summary of Results Achieved (from October 2023 to October 2024)
The Conserving Aquatic Biodiversity Project in Blue Economy achieved several significant outcomes, both expected and unexpected, during its implementation period. These results span across governance, capacity building, gender inclusivity, and environmental conservation.
Policy Alignment and Capacity Building: (i) Assisted countries such as Tunisia, Djibouti, and Uganda in aligning their national policies with global aquatic biodiversity conservation frameworks and (ii) Developed a mechanism for effective participation of African stakeholders in Continental and Global Fora on aquatic biodiversity conservation and environmental management.
Strengthened Regional and Transboundary Collaboration: (i) Facilitated the development of mechanisms for the management of transboundary marine ecosystem, such as the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for joint management of marine conservation areas between Kenya and Tanzania; (ii) Supported Benin and Togo in establishing transboundary Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) processes and the Northern Mozambique Channel region in developing a regional MSP vision and roadmap; (iii) In collaboration with the Fisheries Commission for the Gulf of Guinea (COREP), the Project supported the Republic of Congo and the Republic of Gabon to enhance effective joint governance systems for transboundary marine protected areas and (iv)supported the Republic of Congo and the Democratic Republic of Congo to develop harmonized strategies for transboundary management of shared marine ecosystems in the Gulf of Guinea.
Enhanced Monitoring, Control, and Surveillance (MCS): (i) Supported the operationalized the SADC Regional MCS Coordination Centre, including the inauguration of its Board of Directors. Procured and distributed MCS equipment to countries in the Gulf of Guinea to combat Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing.
Gender Mainstreaming: (i) Developed a continental strategy for gender mainstreaming in aquatic biodiversity conservation and environmental management that was endorsed by the African Heads of States and Governments; (ii) Supported Ethiopia, Malawi, and Côte d'Ivoire in developing gender inclusive strategies for aquatic biodiversity conservation and (iii) Drafted a gender sensitive management plan for the Dusornu Community Resource Management Area in Ghana and in East London, South Africa.
Climate Change Mitigation: (i) Conducted a study on the negative impact of climate change on aquatic biodiversity and environment; (ii) Supported 5 Member States, Gabon, Kenya, Nigeria, Egypt and Angola to pilot guidelines on sustainable marine and coastal tourism and mining to ensure biodiversity and environmental conservation and (iii) Collaborated with Zanzibar stakeholders on seaweed farming to support blue ecosystem restoration and sustainable livelihoods.
2.Unexpected Results
Increased Stakeholder Buy-In: The involvement of high-level policymakers, such as Members of Parliament in Kenya and Tanzania, demonstrated unanticipated political support for the joint management of transboundary aquatic resources.
CrossSectoral Impact: Beyond aquatic conservation, initiatives like the Gazi Bay mangrove restoration project inspired broader community engagement in climate adaptation and introduced innovative livelihood opportunities, such as mangrove based enterprises.
Emergent Partnerships: Collaboration with unexpected partners, such as private sector actors in seaweed farming and nonprofits like Blue Wild Coast in South Africa, expanded the project's scope and influence.
Reputational Boost: The project facilitated notable successes in regional governance, improving the reputation of implementing organizations like AU-IBAR and fostering trust among stakeholders.
These outcomes underscore the project's adaptive management and its contributions to aquatic biodiversity conservation in Africa.
